jobLines.text: List 3 flights from Boston to Chicago

goal:
Do the job below from the input files, then write one JSON file per numbered line.

The input files (label: file):
  - flights: input/flights.txt

For each numbered job line N, write ONE file output/steps/N.json: a JSON object with exactly these keys.
  "text"  — your answer for that line, as a string.
  "cites" — an object: for each input you drew on, its label as the key and a list of {"claim", "quote"} as the value.
            "claim" is one thing your text relies on; "quote" is words copied EXACTLY from that input (spacing and
            ** or __ marks do not matter). Every number in a claim must also appear in its quote.
  In each claim, copy every number, time and price exactly as the input writes it (for example "9:27 AM", not "09:27"),
  because the check matches the numbers in your claim against your quote.
A job line the brief below marks as a FACTS line is different: its file holds ONLY {"results": [{"quote": "...", "values":
{"<fact>": "<value>"}}]} — one result per thing found, one quote copied exactly from the text of that one result, the values written as the quote
writes them; no "text" and no "cites". A line the brief marks as a TEXT line keeps "text" (free words), and every number in it
must be copied from a quote of an earlier facts line.
Write nothing outside output/, and never edit the files under input/. The file must be complete, valid JSON: a file cut
off before its closing brace counts as not written.

The job, line by line:
1. List 3 flights from Boston to Chicago
   rule: under $450; not a red-eye; nonstop

Job line 1 is a FACTS line. Write output/steps/1.json as {"results": [{"quote": "...", "values": {...}}]} and nothing else — no "text", no "cites".
  One result per thing you find in the input "flights": exactly 3 results.
  "quote": ONE quote per result, copied exactly from that result's own text in the input (at most 4000 characters) — never joined from two results.
  "values": one entry per fact below, written exactly as the quote writes it (for example "9:27 AM", not "09:27"; "389", not "389.00").
    - MaxPrice — an amount in US dollars, right after "From", must be under 450 US dollars
    - DepartureWindow — a time, right after "Departure time:", must be between 5:00 AM and 10:00 PM
    - Stops — a number, right after "StaticText", must be at most 0
    - LeaveAirport — words, right after "Leaves"
    - ArriveAirport — words, right after "O"

The plan the person confirmed: Three results, each with a price under 450 US dollars, a departure time in the AI's proposed range between 5:00 AM and 10:00 PM, a stop count of 0 or fewer as the AI's proposal, and quotes naming the departure and arrival airports as \"flights\" writes them.

parts.text: List 3 flights from Boston to Chicago — the input holds no ranking or cap that fixes the list at exactly 3, so only the facts per result are held

notes: The look's own labels were used instead of the person's words: "Leaves" for the departure airport (seen "Boston Logan International Airport") and "O" for the arrival airport (seen "Hare International Airport").
The person's rule "not a red-eye" is carried as a departure-time range between 5:00 AM and 10:00 PM — that range is my proposal for them to check; the input holds no "red-eye" word.
The person's rule "nonstop" is carried as a stop count of 0 or fewer read from the label "StaticText" — that number is my proposal for them to check; the input holds no "nonstop" word.
The price limit "under $450" is the person's own number, read from the label "From" in US dollars.
The count of 3 is enforced only as 3 results in output/steps/1.json; nothing in the input ranks or caps the list at exactly 3, so which 3 flights appear and in what order is not checked.
The input's origin/destination labels ("Where from?", "Where to?") were not found, so "Boston to Chicago" is only reflected through the quoted airport names.
